items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon 出来了。Argon 9 月 30 日宣布、10 月 13 日放出，Carbon 10 月 28 日宣布、11 月 10 日才对所有付费开发者开放，看着是四周一个旗舰。可 Google 5 月说好 6 月出的
items.summary:
Gemini 4 Carbon 出来了。Argon 9 月 30 日宣布、10 月 13 日放出，Carbon 10 月 28 日宣布、11 月 10 日才对所有付费开发者开放，看着是四周一个旗舰。可 Google 5 月说好 6 月出的 3.5 Pro 被直接取消了，Reuters 10 月 1 日报的，Bloomberg 报道原因是编码成绩没达标，DeepMind 也换了管理层，我觉得这个节奏更像补课。再看 Antigravity 在 JetBrains 调查里工作中使用率 6%，Claude Code 是 39%，Google 靠低价抢人也说得通。

Google 10 月 28 日的对比表里，Terminal-Bench 4.0 是 Carbon 65.2%，GPT-6 Astra 59.1%，Opus 5.5 59.6%；256k 到 1M 长上下文的 GraphWalks 是 96.2% 对 71.8% 和 66.8%，这项是 Google 自己跑的；FrontierSWE 2 它 61.2%，输给 Astra 的 65.5% 和 Opus 的 62.3%，OSWorld-2.1 的 81.5% 也输给 Opus 的 87.2%。而且表里的对手是 Fable 5.1，11 月 9 日刚出的 Fable 5.2 不在里面。

独立榜单更冷静。Artificial Analysis 综合指数 Fable 5.2 是 65，Carbon 60，HLE-Diamond 是 80% 对 69%；不过 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上 Carbon 的 65 反过来高于 Fable 5.2 的 60。它的编码 Agent 指数 59，Claude Code 配 Opus 5.5 是 62。AA-Omniscience（知识可靠性）Fable 5.2 是 67，Carbon 54。LMArena 人类投票 Carbon 1526，跟 Argon 的 1522 在误差内打平，只有 4282 票，是预览值，Fable 5.2 还没评分。CursorBench 上 Carbon 以 60.4% 排第一，我只当其中一个参考。

它的长项在读图和读长文档。上下文是 100 万 token，输入输出共用；Google 自己的表里读图表的 Chartography 是 72.5% 对 Opus 5.5 的 66.3%，它和 Artificial Analysis 合作做的多模态知识 Agent 基准排第二，仅次于 Fable 5.2，每任务成本不到第一名的六分之一；Gray Swan 的间接提示注入测试攻击成功率 0%，Google 说这是第一个做到的模型。这几项都是 Google 自己公布的数字。

价格是 $2/$10 每百万 token，只有 Fable 5.2（$8/$40）的四分之一，但只到 11 月 30 日，12 月 1 日起 $4/$20，Argon 也一样，到时候是 Fable 5.2 的一半，跟 GPT-5.6 Sol 现在的价格持平。Artificial Analysis 算每任务成本用的就是 $4/$20 的标准价，Carbon high 得 60 分花 $7.76，Fable 5.2 high 得 62 分花 $9.08，max 得 65 分要 $26.54。按涨价后的价格算，Carbon 比 Fable 5.2 high 便宜约 15%，分数低 2 分。

缺点是慢。Artificial Analysis 测 high 档首个答案要等约 67 秒，跑一个任务 23 到 26 分钟；Plotly 自己跑数据分析题，Carbon 单题中位数 93 秒，是 Argon 23 秒的四倍。Google 自己也说多数编码和知识工作用 Argon 就行，Carbon 留给最难的活。至于「长任务」，METR 9 月起就不更新任务时长了，最后测的 Mythos Preview 在 50% 成功率下约 17 小时、80% 下约 3 小时，Carbon 没有这类独立数据。我觉得它适合读几百页文档、看图表蓝图这类不赶时间的活，需要来回交互的就别选它。 https://t.co/AvgZXR6jfL

items.title: Google turned on Gemini 4 Carbon yesterday and buried the real story in the fine print: introductory pricing of $2 per m
items.summary:
Google turned on Gemini 4 Carbon yesterday and buried the real story in the fine print: introductory pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens jumps to $4 and $20 the moment November ends. A model good enough to ship at a discount, priced to double the second the launch headlines fade.

What it's actually good at is the interesting part. Carbon tops CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity's WANDR and Zapier's AutomationBench, and Google says it finds zero day vulnerabilities in major SaaS products within two hours of internal testing. On defense it blocked 99% of an adaptive red team's attack paths and scored a clean 0% attack success rate on Gray Swan's prompt injection benchmark. Offense and defense, same model, same week.

That pairing is where this gets uncomfortable rather than impressive. A model this good at finding exploits is, by definition, a model this good at writing them. Google's answer is a Fairwind Program giving vetted defenders early access, which only helps if attackers don't get their own frontier model with the same two hour turnaround.

Zoom out and the cybersecurity benchmark race has gotten crowded fast. Semgrep's latest numbers put https://t.co/MAWoH6xO1K's GLM-5.3 at roughly Opus 4.8 level on IDOR detection for about a seventh of the cost per finding, $0.15 versus $1.04. Neither touches the actual leaders on that test, Opus 5 at 65.6% and GPT-5.6 Luna at 48%. Carbon wasn't entered in that particular benchmark, but the market shape is clear: a frontier tier racing on raw capability, a value tier racing on cost per finding, and most security teams ending up running both.

My read: the November 30 price jump is the tell. Google rarely discounts a model it isn't a little worried will look expensive next to whatever Anthropic or OpenAI ship in the next few weeks.

https://t.co/qVnDtu3gUj

In December, Trump said he had granted Nvidia approval to sell its second-most powerful chip, the H200, to China under an arrangement that would see 25 percent of sales paid to the US government.

Advertisement

[...] While export controls have spurred contentious debate, their effectiveness has been called into question amid China’s steady advances in AI development.

Authorities and analysts have documented widespread smuggling of restricted chips into China, mainly through Southeast Asia.

THE CEO OF JAPAN'S SOFTBANK JUST ADMITTED OPENAI'S GPT-6 ASTRA FOUND 35,000 NEW SECURITY HOLES IN HIS SYSTEMS. HIS WORDS: "HONESTLY, WE'RE COMPLETELY EXHAUSTED."

June 16: emergency press conference. About 700 SoftBank systems scanned, 10,500 holes found. 3 months of patching followed.

Then: a new scan with "GPT-6 Astra", OpenAI's newest model then. 35,000 NEW holes.

Oct 7: hackers hit its cloud arm through open-source code it had never scanned. 7 minutes from alarm to damage.

Now: attackers probe its systems 600 to 700 million times a month. About double last year.

Yesterday: the CEO said each new AI model finds holes no one knew about. "We can't handle it with human hands alone."

SoftBank's new rule: if anything looks wrong, cut the line, even if service goes down. Cut first. Fix later.

None of this is a forecast. It already happened.

4 days ago, OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber, a security version of GPT-6 Astra, and raised its cyber risk rating from High to CRITICAL. It built working attacks for 948 Linux kernel holes.

Last week in France, hackers stole about €100 million from the bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa. In South Korea, crypto exchange GOPAX froze withdrawals and trading after a hacking threat.

At least 33 countries now tell people to stockpile at home:
🇬🇧 UK: 3 days of food and water, a power bank, cash, an FM radio
🇪🇺 EU: at least 72 hours
🇸🇪 Sweden, 🇳🇴 Norway: a full week
🇩🇪 Germany: up to 10 days
🇫🇷 🇫🇮 🇱🇹 🇱🇻 🇳🇱 🇨🇿: at least 72 hours
🇯🇵 Japan: food and water

Why FM? It works even in a blackout or a cyberattack, when phones and internet die. Britain's emergency advice: stay home, turn on an FM radio.

Britain's cyber chief Richard Horne (NCSC): "When food isn't on the shelves, when lights aren't on, businesses have gone under."

This is the AI cyberattack era. Better safe than sorry.

Follow me now. The day your bank app goes dark is a bad day to start catching up.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary:
Dexterity: Our robots can perform significantly more tasks with greater performance and dexterity — from using everyday tools to handling delicate, flexible objects.
 Reliability: During a real-world proof-of-concept on Mercedes-Benz production lines, our models helped Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid pick and pack automotive parts with a 96% success rate. This could enable robots to take on monotonous work, to enable technicians to focus on complex build tasks. [...] Robots struggle to adapt to new unpredictable environments, our Gemini Robotics models give Apollo the ability to think, reason over multiple steps, and take action adapting to changes. In this proof-of-concept, Apollo 2 autonomously performs automotive kitting: the repetitive, physically taxing task of sorting individual parts from bulk bins into organized trays in the exact order needed for each vehicle on the line. Offloading this monotonous prep work helps keep the assembly line moving, [...] With Gemini Robotics 2.5, we expanded the model capabilities in task breadth, performance, and complexity. We evaluated the model across 200 distinct tasks — such as serving food with tongs, tying a bow on a gift box, and pipetting a liquid. These tasks represent a step toward human-level dexterity by combining a number of skills, including advanced tool use, complex manipulation of deformables, and handling delicate objects with finesse.

items.title: Industrial automation startup Path Robotics raises $300M in funding - SiliconANGLE
items.summary: Path Robotics originally developed Obsidian for large robotic workstations called welding cells. In April, it introduced a four-legged robot called Rove that uses the model to automate shipbuilding tasks. The company says that its software can also be used to make parts for vehicles, power generators, utility poles and other heavy equipment. [...] Path Robotics has developed an AI model that addresses those challenges. Obsidian, as it’s called, is specifically designed to power industrial robots equipped with welding torches. The company says that the model can observe how metal parts change shape during the welding process and adjust its workflow accordingly. Furthermore, it automatically accounts for unexpected part variations. [...] Obsidian monitors the welding workflow using four lasers attached to the torch that it controls. The emitters illuminate the parts being welded together and the reflected light is captured by a pair of cameras. According to Path Robotics, Obsidian collects data not only during the welding process but also before and after each run.

items.title: Aguascalientes students take top robotics prizes
items.summary:
The Aguascalientes team, nicknamed Lanceros Overclock, won the high school division (ages 14 to 20) of Robo Shuttle at ROBOchæmpions, held Saturday and Sunday in the city of Lörrach. 

The competition required the budding scientists to work in teams of two or four to build and program autonomous robots that would perform predetermined tasks. (Phaenovum) [...] Overall, 16 students from Aguascalientes competed, but the names of the winners were not included in official results.

According to organizer Phaenovum — a student research center in Lörrach, Germany — the inaugural competition hosted teams from Mexico and Egypt in addition to regional competitors. It succeeded RoboRAVE Germany, a previous local version of RoboRAVE.

The organizer published results in five categories spanning races, robot duels, transport tasks and autonomous firefighting. [...] One challenge required robots to extinguish a candle flame autonomously.

Teams prepared and tested their robots Saturday before Sunday’s judging, awards ceremony and public demonstrations.
